text: περιαιρέω, (a) I strip off, I strip from, I take away; (b) I cast off, cut adrift, Ac. xxvii 40; in Ac. xxviii 13, if the text be right, the word must be rendered in the same way, I cast off, I cast loose.
gloss: I strip off, I strip from, I take away

text: περιάπτω, I light, ignite.
περιαστράπτω, I flash (gleam) around like lightning.
περιβόλαιον, a wrapper, mantle.
περιδέω, I bind (tie) around.
περιεργάζομαι, I am active around, I am a busybody.
gloss: I am active around, I am a busybody

text: περίεργος, (a) inquisitive, prying, a busybody; (b) curious, magical, Ac. xix 19.
περιέρχομαι, intr. and tr., I go round, I move about (περιερχόμενοι, strolling, Ac. xix 13); I make a circuit, tack, Ac. xxviii 13 (v.l.).
gloss: I go round, I move about

text: περιέχω, (a) I contain (of a book containing subject matter): hence, impersonal, it stands (has its content) thus, 1 Pet. ii 6; (b) I encompass, surround; I get hold of, seize.
περιζώννυμι, I gird round: mid. I gird myself, generally for active work or travel.
περίθεσις, a putting around (or on).
περιίστημι: in intr. tenses, I surround; I stand clear of, 2 Tim. ii 16, Tit. iii 9.
περικάθαρμα, a rinsing of a dirty vessel.
gloss: a rinsing of a dirty vessel

text: περικαλύπτω, I veil round, I cover over; I conceal.
gloss: I veil round, I cover over

text: περικεφαλαία, a helmet.
περικρατής, mastering, gaining control over.
περικρύπτω, I conceal, hide (by putting something around it).
gloss: I conceal, hide (by putting something around it)

text: περικυκλόω, I encircle, invest.
περιλάμπω, I shine around.
περιλείπω, I leave behind.
περίλυπος, deeply pained (grieved).
περιμένω, I await the happening of something.
gloss: I await the happening of something

text: πέριξ, round about, in the neighbourhood.
περιοικέω, I dwell around (near).
περίοικος, neighbouring; a neighbour.
περιούσιος, of (for) one's own (special, private) possession.
περιοχή, a clause, sentence, short passage.
περιπείρω, I pierce round about (on all sides).
gloss: I pierce round about (on all sides)

text: περιπίπτω, I fall into, I fall in with, I meet with, I come upon accidentally, I chance upon, I light upon.
gloss: I fall into, I fall in with, I meet with

text: περιποιέομαι, I make my own, I acquire (get) for myself, I gain for myself; in Lk. xvii 33 perhaps, I preserve alive.
gloss: I make my own, I acquire (get) for myself

text: περιποίησις, acquiring, obtaining, possessing, possession, ownership.
περιρήγνυμι, I rend all round, I tear off.
gloss: I rend all round, I tear off

text: περισπάω, I distract, trouble greatly.
περισσεία, excrescence; superabundance, superfluity.
περίσσευμα, what is in excess; overflow, superabundance, superfluity.
περισσῶς, exceedingly, so perhaps Ac. xxvi 11; but usually more (cf. περισσός), with reference to what precedes.
περιτρέπω, I turn round, I turn, change.
gloss: I turn round, I turn, change

text: περιτρέχω, I run round (around).
περιφέρω, I carry around (about); I swing round, Eph. iv 14.
περιφρονέω, I lightly esteem; I despise.
περίχωρος, neighbouring; ἡ περίχωρος (sc. γῆ), the neighbouring country, the neighbourhood, surroundings.
περίψημα, that which is scraped off round anything, a scraping.
gloss: that which is scraped off round anything, a scraping

text: περπερεύομαι, I show myself off; I am boastful (a braggart).
Περσίς, Persis, name of a Christian lady in Rome.
gloss: Persis, name of a Christian lady in Rome

text: πέρυσι, adverb, the previous year, last year.
πετρώδης, rocky.
πήγανον, rue, a plant used for flavouring, garnishing dishes, &c.
gloss: rue, a plant used for flavouring, garnishing dishes

text: πήγνυμι, I fix, pitch; I erect.
πηδάλιον, a helm, rudder.
πηλίκος, how large, how great.
πηλός, mud; clay.
πήρα, a bag (to hold food, &c.), a wallet, a travelling bag, perhaps especially a collecting bag (such as beggar-priests of pagan cults carried).
gloss: a bag (to hold food, &c.), a wallet, a travelling bag

text: πῆχυς, the fore-arm; hence, a cubit, about a foot and a half: used as a measurement of time in Mt. vi 27 (Lk. xii 25), to indicate any extension.
πιέζω, I press down.
πιθανολογία, persuasive speech.
πικραίνω, I make bitter (tart, sour): mid. I am embittered, I show quick temper.
πικρία, bitterness, sourness; hence met., an embittered (resentful) spirit, which refuses reconciliation, Eph. iv 31.
πικρός, bitter, lit. and met.
πικρῶς, bitterly.
πίμπρημι, I cause to swell: passive, I become inflamed, I am swollen.
πινακίδιον, a little waxed tablet, on which to write with iron pen.
gloss: a little waxed tablet, on which to write with iron pen

text: πίναξ, a flat dish.
πιότης, fatness.
Πισιδία, Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor, being the south-western part of the Roman province Galatia.
gloss: Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor

text: πιστικός, probably = genuine, pure.
πλανήτης, wandering (probably of shooting stars).
πλάνος, adj., misleading, deceiving: as subst. a deceiver.
πλάξ, a tablet.
πλάσμα, a moulded thing; a created thing, a creature.
πλάσσω, I mould out of clay; I create.
πλαστός (finctus), made up, fictitious.
πλάτος, breadth.
πλατύνω, I broaden, I make broad: met., of the growth of tenderness and love, 2 Cor. vi 11, 13.
πλατύς, broad.
πλέγμα, plaiting, braiding, dressing the hair.
πλέκω, I plait.
πλεονέκτης, a greedy, covetous, rapacious, acquisitive, self-aggrandizing person; a defrauder, one who tramples on the rights of others.
gloss: a greedy, covetous, rapacious, acquisitive, self-aggrandizing person

text: πλευρά, a side of a human being.
gloss: a side of a human being

text: πλέω, I travel by sea, I sail, voyage.
gloss: I travel by sea, I sail, voyage

text: πλήκτης, a striker; a pugnacious person.
πλημμύρα, a flooding, flood.
πληροφορία, full assurance, conviction (confidence).
πλησμονή, repletion, satiety.
πλήσσω, I strike.
πλοιάριον, (a little boat, hence) a boat.
πλόος, a voyage.
note: headword printed in uncontracted form πλόος

text: πλουσίως, richly; lavishly.
πλουτίζω, I enrich.
πλύνω, I wash.
πνευματικῶς, spiritually, in a spiritual way; from a spiritual point of view.
πνέω, I blow: τῇ πνεούσῃ (sc. αὔρᾳ, breeze).
πνίγω, I choke, throttle, strangle; hence I drown, Mk. v 13.
πνικτός, strangled (i.e. killed without letting out the blood).
gloss: strangled (i.e. killed without letting out the blood)

text: πνοή, (a) breath, Ac. xvii 25; (b) gust, breeze, wind, Ac. ii 2. (Cf. Augustine, De Natura et Origine Animae I 14 § 19).
ποδήρης (talaris) (properly an adjective in the expression χιτὼν ποδήρης), a tunic or robe reaching the feet.
gloss: a tunic or robe reaching the feet

text: ποίημα (concrete), creation, workmanship, handiwork; plur. pieces of work.
ποίησις, doing.
ποιητής, (a) a ‘maker’, a poet, Ac. xvii 28 (the reference is to Epimenides’ Minos); (b) a doer, a carrier out.
ποίμνη, a flock; herd (of goats perhaps, in 1 Cor. ix 7).
ποίμνιον, a little flock: hence, of men.
πολεμέω, I war, carry on war.
πολιτάρχης, a politarch, a city-magistrate (a special, characteristically Macedonian, title of the chief magistrates (5 or 6 in number) of Thessalonica and a few other cities).
πολιτεία (ciuitas), (a) commonwealth, polity; citizen body, Eph. ii 12; (b) (the Roman) citizenship, citizen-rights, franchise, Ac. xxii 28.

πολίτευμα (properly, that which one does as citizen), the constitution; citizenship, franchise; the state, the community, the commonwealth. The word sometimes means a colony of foreigners, whose organization is a miniature copy of the πολιτεία at home, and this gives excellent sense in Phil. iii 20.
πολιτεύομαι (a characteristic Greek idea), I live the life of a citizen; I live as a member of a (citizen) body; I fulfil corporate duties: in Phil. i 27 some take simply of manner of life.
gloss: I live the life of a citizen

text: πολίτης (ciuis), a citizen: a fellow-citizen, Lk. xix 14, Heb. viii 11.
πολλαπλασίων (multiplex), manifold, many times over.
πολυλογία, much-speaking, loquaciousness, volubility.
πολυμερῶς, in many portions (one at one time, another at another, and so on).
πολυποίκιλος, much varied, very varied.
πολύσπλαγχνος, full of tender feeling (a Hebraistic idiom, the bowels [σπλάγχνα, which see] being regarded as the seat of compassion and pity, &c.).
πολυτελής, expensive, costly: hence precious, valuable, 1 Pet. iii 4.
πολύτιμος, costly, expensive: hence valuable, precious, 1 Pet. i 7.
πολυτρόπως, in many ways, under many aspects (with reference probably to different laws or injunctions).
gloss: in many ways, under many aspects

text: πόμα, drink.
πονηρία (malignitas), the active exercise of vicious propensity, malignity, wickedness: plur. iniquities, Mk. vii 22, Ac. iii 26.
gloss: the active exercise of vicious propensity

text: πόνος, labour, toil; trouble.
Ποντικός, belonging to Pontus (which see).
Πόντιος, Pontius, the second or gentile name of Pilate.
gloss: Pontius, the second or gentile name of Pilate

text: Πόντος, Pontus, a Roman province in the north of Asia Minor, bordering on the Black Sea, governed along with Bithynia.
gloss: Pontus, a Roman province in the north of Asia Minor

text: Πόπλιος, the Greek form of the Latin name Publius (originally the same in form as the Greek form); a governor of Malta.
gloss: the Greek form of the Latin name Publius

text: πορεία, a journey.
πορθέω, I devastate, lay waste: hence, I bring destruction upon, I destroy.
πορισμός (quaestus), a means of gain, a way of making a living, a livelihood, a living.
gloss: a means of gain, a way of making a living

text: Πόρκιος, Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus.
gloss: Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus

text: πόρρω (procul), far, at a distance.
πόρρωθεν, from a long distance, Heb. xi 13: hence (cf. ἔξωθεν), at a long distance, far away, Lk. xvii 12.
πορφύρα, a purple robe, purple; a red-coloured cloak, such as common soldiers wore, Mk. xv 17, 20.
πορφυρόπωλις, a woman dealer in purple-dyed garments.
gloss: a woman dealer in purple-dyed garments

text: ποσάκις, how many times?, how often?
πόσις, drinking: hence, concrete, drink, as perhaps in all N.T. passages (certainly in John vi 55).
ποταμοφόρητος, river-borne, carried off by a river.
gloss: river-borne, carried off by a river

text: ποταπός, (from what country?, in what country born?, and then) of what sort?, how fashioned? (hence, practically, how great?, 1 John iii 1).
πότερον (utrum), whether.
Ποτίολοι, Puteoli (now Pozzuoli), the great harbour for traffic with Alexandria, &c., on the Bay of Naples.
πότος, a drinking bout.
Πούδης (Latin), Pudens, a Christian man in Rome.
gloss: Pudens, a Christian man in Rome

text: πραγματεία, business, business transaction.
πραγματεύομαι, I do business, I trade.

πραιτώριον (Latin praetorium, meaning originally, the quarters (residence) of the general), (a) the official residence of the procurator, which in Jerusalem was the palace of Herod on the west side of the city; (b) personally, the imperial guard, the praetorian guard, or perhaps, the law officers of the Crown, Phil. i 13.
gloss: the official residence of the procurator

text: πράκτωρ, (usually, a collector of revenue, but in Lk.) an officer (usher) of the court.
πρᾶξις, (a) abstr., conduct; function, Rom. xii 4; (b) concrete, in plur. doings, deeds.
πρασιά, a vegetable or flower bed: πρασιαὶ πρασιαί, colloquial type of phrase, like vegetable or flower beds, referring to the rectangular arrangement of the groups.
πραϋπάθεια, meekness (gentleness) of spirit.
πραΰς, meek, gentle.
πρέπω, I suit: generally impersonal, or with neuter pronoun as subject, πρέπει, πρέπον ἐστίν, it is becoming, it is fitting.
πρεσβεία, an embassy, delegation.
πρεσβεύω (especially, I am on embassy to the Emperor), I am an ambassador.

πρεσβυτέριον, (a) amongst the Jews, a college of elders, who supervised the worship, &c., of the synagogue; hence, the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem; (b) the Christian analogue, a college of elders of a particular church.
πρεσβύτης, an old man.
πρεσβῦτις, an old woman.
πρηνής (a medical term, denoting a disease, and corresponding to πίμπρημι, which see), swollen up, inflamed.
πρίζω, I saw, I saw through.

Πρῖσκα, Πρίσκιλλα, Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.
note: headword printed with circumflex (Πρῖσκα), followed by Πρίσκιλλα

text: προαιρέομαι, I choose deliberately.
προαιτιάομαι, I make a prior accusation.
προακούω, I hear beforehand.
προαμαρτάνω, I sin previously.
προαύλιον, a forecourt, a courtyard in the front part of a building.
gloss: a forecourt, a courtyard in the front part of a building

text: προβάλλω, (a) tr. I put forward; (b) I put forth shoots, I sprout, burst into leaf, Lk. xxi 30.
προβατικός, connected with sheep: προβατική (sc. πύλη) the Sheep Gate of Jerusalem: if κολυμβήθρᾳ be read, προβατικῇ agrees with it.
προβιβάζω, I instruct.
προβλέπομαι, I provide; I resolve on.
προγίνομαι, I happen (come about) previously.
πρόγνωσις, foreknowledge.
πρόγονος, an ancestor.
προγράφω, (a) I write previously (aforetime), Rom. xv 4, Jude 4; I write above (already), Eph. iii 3: (b) I evidently pourtray or I placard, advertise, Gal. iii 1.
πρόδηλος, perfectly clear (evident).
προδίδωμι, I give previously.
προδότης, (a) a betrayer; (b) traitorous, treacherous, 2 Tim. iii 4.
πρόδρομος, a forerunner.
προελπίζω, I hope before another, I am the first to hope.
gloss: I hope before another, I am the first to hope

text: προενάρχομαι, I begin earlier (previously).
προεπαγγέλλομαι, I promise beforehand.
